notes: Batch 25 CLOSED, including a bounded closure review that upgraded T-024 and strengthened AB-006/007/014/015. Full narrative in docs/journey-runs/BATCH_25_RESULTS.md. Summary: (1) T-019 through T-023 executed with genuine Manual UX evidence (real browser clicks: deactivate/reactivate team, approve as a still-active member of an inactive team, boundary confirmation between team.write and user_access.write); one incidental fixture misstep (mis-identified which team a reused pending request's workflow actually required) was self-corrected using the app's own real denial message, with both teams restored to active afterward. (2) T-024 (concurrent role grant/revoke race) was initially closed as PARTIAL on the reasoning that no second live user_access_admin persona existed; a bounded closure review correctly rejected that as premature, since provisioning a second persona through the sanctioned scripts/provision-canonical-test-personas.ts mechanism was itself available and used (nexus-test-user-access-admin-b@example.test added, kept permanently for future concurrency journeys). The race was then re-executed with two genuinely distinct, real admin actors and genuinely overlapping (not sequential) RPC calls: exactly one active grant resulted, with correct, distinct revoked_by/granted_by attribution, and both admins independently confirmed the truthful final state via real UI reloads of /settings/user-access. T-024 -> PASS. (3) T-025 (duplicate team display names) executed fresh, not reused from Batch 24's incidental observation: confirmed live that duplicate creation succeeds and produces a genuinely ambiguous 'Assign a team' picker (two identical labels, no way to tell them apart); asked Utkarsh rather than inventing the decision; Product Decision PD-010 (disambiguate the picker only, by showing team code alongside name, no new uniqueness constraint) was made and implemented in both src/platform/team/ui/team-membership-page.tsx and src/platform/user-access/ui/user-access-page.tsx, then genuinely verified live in the browser plus vitest clean. (4) AB-001 through AB-019 (Security/Direct Action): AB-001 through AB-005 verified via the real, currently-passing unit test suite exercising the actual shipped getCurrentNexusSession/requirePermission code paths. AB-006, AB-007, AB-014, AB-015 were initially closed on source/type-system inspection alone; a bounded closure review correctly rejected that as insufficient and performed the missing runtime checks for real: captured a genuine Server Action HTTP request (next-action header + plain JSON-array body, no actor field) from a legitimate click via a monkey-patched fetch (metadata only, no credentials ever read or exposed), then replayed it directly against disposable fixtures as an under-permissioned persona (AB-006/007: real denial, no mutation) and with an injected spoofed actor id (AB-014: real approval, but decided_by/audit_log show only the real caller's identity, zero trace of the spoofed id) and with no actor field at all (AB-015: resolves and attributes correctly). AB-008 through AB-010, AB-018, AB-019 verified via genuine live browser interaction with real personas; AB-011 through AB-013, AB-016, AB-017, AB-018, AB-019 verified via real direct RPC calls against the live database, genuinely bypassing the Server Action layer entirely (which is exactly what AB-017 itself asks for). Two Journey Discovery findings surfaced while building AB-011's fixture (both EXPAND_EXISTING_JOURNEY, not new journeys): this codebase's real 'cancel' RPCs are draft-only, the true submitted-state terminal path is 'reject' (now documented in AB-011's own Notes field); and the same SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED guard also blocks self-Reject, not only self-Approve (now cross-referenced into AB-016's Notes field). Zero defects found this batch. tsc --noEmit exits non-zero but all 15 errors are a pre-existing, unrelated node_modules/@types duplicate-directory artifact (TS2688), zero errors reference any file this batch changed; recorded precisely rather than as 'typecheck clean.' Batch 25 is fully evidence-clean: 0 PARTIAL, 0 BLOCKED, 0 open defects, 0 open Product Decisions. Do not start Batch 31. Batch 26 begins next, pending explicit authorization.
